mainTopic: A גט must be written לשמה, for a specific woman. The גמרא finds the source in the פסוק, discusses same-name documents, and asks whether invalid גיטין still forbid a woman to a כהן.
overview: The משנה finishes its list of invalid גיטין. A גט written for one wife cannot divorce his other wife with the same name, and a גט written 'for whichever wife I choose' is invalid for both. The גמרא explains that the משנה's first case is about scribes practicing, proven from the word מקרין. A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל shows how each 'יתר מיכן' goes one step further. The גמרא finds each step in the words of the פסוק: ספר כריתות, וכתב, and לה (לשמה). The last case teaches אין ברירה. רבא learns a rule about two people with the same name collecting a שטר חוב, but אביי pushes it away: the משנה works only because of עדי מסירה, following רבי אלעזר. Finally, רב and שמואל argue whether these invalid גיטין still forbid a woman to a כהן. שמואל's view fits his rule that an invalid גט or חליצה is 'פסול ופוסל'.

steps.title: Two wives with the same name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a גט written to divorce the older wife cannot be used to divorce the younger wife, even though both have the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, if a man had two wives with the same name and wrote a גט to divorce the older one, he may not use it to divorce the younger one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another case to its list of invalid גיטין. A גט written for one wife does not work for the other wife, even when their names match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the words in the גט fit the younger wife perfectly, it was written for the older one. A גט must be written for the specific woman it divorces, so a matching name is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Moreover; going even further than the previous case
Their names are the same
The older wife / the younger wife

steps.whyThisMatters: This case is stronger than earlier ones. It is the same husband and the same name, and still the גט is invalid, because it was written for a different woman.

phrases.english: Moreover,
if he had two wives
and their names were the same,
and he wrote [a גט] to divorce the older one,
he may not divorce the younger one with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר מִיכֵּן – הָיוּ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of גיטין that were not written for the right woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written for the older wife cannot divorce the younger wife who has the same name.

steps.title: A גט for whichever wife he chooses
steps.stepSummary: If the husband tells the scribe to write a גט that he will later use for whichever wife he wants, the גט is invalid for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, if he told the scribe: 'Write a גט, and I will divorce whichever wife I want with it,' it is invalid to divorce with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last and strongest case. The husband did not pick a wife when the גט was written, so it cannot be used for either of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 the גט was at least written for one specific woman. Here it was written for no particular woman. That is why it fails for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe
For whichever one I want
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: A גט must be written for one specific woman at the time it is written. Choosing her later does not help.

phrases.english: Moreover,
if he said to the scribe: "Write,
and whichever one I want, I will divorce [with it]",
it is invalid to divorce with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step further than step 1. There the גט was written for a specific wife; here it was written for no specific wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written without choosing a specific wife is invalid for both wives.

steps.title: What is the first case of the משנה about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the later case: a man wrote a גט for his wife and changed his mind. It then asks what the earlier case of the scribes must be about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he wrote a גט to divorce his wife and changed his mind, etc.' If so, what is the first case dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion. It quotes the later case of the משנה, then asks what the earlier case is about. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later case is a גט really written for a divorce, which another man with the same name then wants to use. In the earlier case, a man heard scribes reading out a גט with his and his wife's names. If that is also a real גט written for someone else, the two cases look the same. So the גמרא asks what the earlier case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
He changed his mind
The first part of the משנה
What is it dealing with?

steps.confusionAlert: רישא here means the earlier case in this משנה, about the scribes reading out names. It is not the cases in steps 1 and 2.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְנִמְלַךְ וְכוּ׳:
phrases.english: "If he wrote [a גט] to divorce his wife and changed his mind, etc."
phrases.notes: This is the later case in the משנה: another man from his town with the same names wants to use that גט.

phrases.english: But then, what is the first part [of the משנה] dealing with?
phrases.notes: The first part is the man in the market who heard scribes reading out a גט with his and his wife's names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of how the cases in the משנה are set up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is the רישא about, so that it is different from the later case?
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the משנה lists both cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both cases are a real גט written for another man, the רישא teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The first case is about scribes practicing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the first case is about scribes who were only practicing writing a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We are dealing with scribes who write [גיטין] to practice.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. In the first case, the גט was written only as practice, not for anyone's divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two cases are different. The first case is a practice גט, written for no divorce at all. The later case is a גט written for a real divorce, just for a different man. The משנה teaches that both are invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribes
Who are practicing or learning
We are dealing with

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
We are dealing with scribes who are practicing [writing גיטין].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּסוֹפְרִין הָעֲשׂוּיִין לְהִתְלַמֵּד עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא is about a practice גט, written for no divorce at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases looked like a real גט written for someone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is a practice גט; the later case is a real גט written for a different man.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'dictating'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports רב פפא from the משנה's wording: it says the scribes were 'dictating', not just 'reading'. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording is exact too. The משנה says 'scribes dictating,' not 'scribes reading.' Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings proof from the exact wording of the משנה that רב פפא is right. The גמרא closes with 'learn from this.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: מקרין means reading aloud to someone else, like a teacher dictating to students. קורין would just mean reading. Because the משנה chose מקרין, the scene is a lesson, which fits scribes practicing.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is exact too; the text supports this
Dictating; reading aloud to others
Reading
Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The first case is a practice גט, proven from the word מקרין. The later case is a real גט written for another man. Both are invalid because neither was written for this couple.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
The wording is exact too,
since it teaches "scribes dictating,"
and it does not teach "scribes reading";
learn from this [that it is so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רב פפא's answer from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reading that the רישא is about scribes practicing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה says מקרין (dictating), not קורין (reading).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רישא is about a practice גט, and the גמרא accepts this with שמע מינה.

steps.title: What does 'Moreover' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means each time it says 'יתר מיכן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'Moreover'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'יתר מיכן' in the משנה is coming to add. This question sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה moves from one case to the next with 'יתר מיכן', which means each new case should go further than the one before. The גמרא wants to know exactly what each new case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Moreover / even more than this': a word showing that the next case goes further
What?

phrases.english: What is 'Moreover'?
phrases.notes: The משנה uses this word each time it moves to a harder case: practicing scribes, the man who changed his mind, two wives, then 'whichever I want'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case of the practicing scribes is clear (Steps 4-5), the גמרא looks at how the משנה builds from that case to the later ones.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea each 'יתר מיכן' case adds beyond the case before it.

steps.title: Each case goes one level further
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains that each case in the משנה adds something new, and each one is still פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Not only this גט, written not for divorce at all, is invalid. Even this one, written for divorce, is invalid. Not only this one, written not for his own divorce, is invalid. Even this one, written for his own divorce, is invalid. Not only this one, not written for this wife's divorce, is invalid. Even this one, written for 'this' wife's divorce, is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that lays out three levels. At each level, the new case is closer to a kosher גט than the one before it, and it is still פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Level 1: the practice גט was not for divorce at all, but even a גט written for a real divorce (and then the husband changed his mind) cannot be used by someone else. Level 2: that one was not for this man's own divorce, but even a גט written for his own divorce cannot be used for his other wife with the same name. Level 3: that one was written for a different wife, but even a גט written for 'whichever wife I choose' is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
For the sake of divorce
His own
Invalid
'Not only this, but even this': a pattern that builds from an easier case to a harder one

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of 'not לשמה': not for divorce at all, not for his divorce, and not for this specific wife. Each one is פסול, and each goes a step further than the last.

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶה – שֶׁנִּכְתַּב שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין;
phrases.english: Not only this one, which was written not for the sake of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַף זֶה – שֶׁנִּכְתַּב לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין, פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: but even this one, which was written for the sake of divorce, is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the man who wrote a גט for his wife and changed his mind. Someone else can't use it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זֶה – שֶׁנִּכְתַּב שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין דִּידֵיהּ;
phrases.english: And not only this one, which was written not for the sake of his own divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַף זֶה – שֶׁנִּכְתַּב לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין דִּידֵיהּ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: but even this one, which was written for the sake of his own divorce, is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the man with two wives of the same name, from Step 1.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זֶה – שֶׁלֹּא נִכְתַּב לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין הָא;
phrases.english: And not only this one, which was not written for the sake of this wife's divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַף זֶה – שֶׁנִּכְתַּב לְשׁוּם גֵּירוּשִׁין הָא, פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: but even this one, which was written for the sake of 'this' wife's divorce, is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is 'whichever wife I want', from Step 2. In a sense it was written for her, but it wasn't fixed to her alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each 'יתר מיכן' adds a case that is closer to a valid גט than the one before it, and it is still פסול.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind these levels of disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where in the תורה we learn these rules. This question sets up the reading of the פסוק in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave three levels of disqualification. Now the גמרא wants to show that the פסוק needs words that teach each level.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? / What is the source?
Reason

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the תורה source behind the levels listed in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words of the פסוק teach each level of disqualification.

steps.title: Why the word 'וכתב' is needed
steps.stepSummary: 'ונתן ספר כריתות בידה' alone would only rule out the practice גט. 'וכתב' is needed to rule out the גט of the man who changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'and he gives a scroll of severance in her hand', I would have said it only excludes the first case, which was not done for severance at all. But if a man wrote a גט to divorce his wife and changed his mind, which was done for severance, I would say it is valid. So the תורה wrote 'and he writes'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the words 'ונתן ספר כריתות בידה' would only rule out the practice גט, so the word 'וכתב' is added to rule out the next case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ספר כריתות' means a document made for cutting off a marriage, so a practice גט is clearly ruled out. A גט written for a real divorce is a 'ספר כריתות', so we might think another man could use it. 'וכתב' teaches that the husband himself must write it (or have it written) for his own divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll of severance: the תורה's name for a גט
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
To exclude
Changed his mind
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה
Valid

phrases.english: If it had written 'and he gives a scroll of severance in her hand',
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

phrases.english: I would have said it is to exclude that first case,
which was not done for the sake of severance;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כָּתַב לְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְנִמְלַךְ,
phrases.english: but if he wrote it to divorce his wife and changed his mind,
which was done for the sake of severance, I would say it is valid;
so the Merciful One wrote: 'and he writes'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב וְנָתַן סֵפֶר כְּרִיתוּת בְּיָדָהּ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering Step 8 by explaining the first two levels from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכתב' teaches that the גט must be written for this husband's own divorce, so a גט written for one man cannot be used by another.

steps.title: Why the word 'לה' is needed
steps.stepSummary: 'וכתב' alone would allow a man with two wives to use one wife's גט for the other. 'לה' teaches that it must be written for her specifically: לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'and he writes', I would have said it only excludes this case, where he is not the one writing it for her. But if he has two wives, where he is the one writing it for her, I would say it is valid. So the תורה wrote 'for her', meaning for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that 'וכתב' alone would not rule out the two-wives case, so the word 'לה' is needed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכתב' only requires that the husband himself writes it, so a man with two wives might think one גט works for either wife. 'לה' adds that the גט must be written for this specific woman. That is the source for the rule of לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: For her sake: written specifically for this woman
He himself
Two wives

steps.whatToRemember: Every word of 'וכתב לה ספר כריתות' teaches something: 'ספר כריתות' means it must be for divorce, 'וכתב' means for his own divorce, and 'לה' means for this specific wife (לשמה).
steps.confusionAlert: The two-wives גט was written by the right husband, for a real divorce. It is still פסול because it was written for the other wife and not לשמה of the wife he now wants to divorce.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source in the תורה for the requirement that a גט be written לשמה, a basic rule throughout מסכת גיטין.

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written only 'and he writes',
I would have said it is to exclude this case,
where he is not the one writing it for her;
phrases.notes: This is the גט of the man who changed his mind, now being used by someone else.

phrases.english: but if he has two wives,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיהוּ קָא כָתֵיב לַהּ – אֵימָא כָּשֵׁר;
phrases.english: where he is the one writing it for her, I would say it is valid;
so the Merciful One wrote: 'for her', meaning for her sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא וְכָתַב הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the פסוק from Step 9 and explains the next level of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לה' teaches that the גט must be written for this specific wife (לשמה), so a man cannot use one wife's גט to divorce his other wife.

steps.title: Why do we need the last case of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs its last case, where a man writes a גט for whichever wife he will later choose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need the last part of the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs its last case. The earlier cases already taught that a גט must be written לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-10 showed that 'לה' requires the גט to be written for her. So a case where the man writes it for whichever wife he later picks seems to add nothing new. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (end clause) of a משנה
Why do I need it? (asking what a line adds)

phrases.english: And why do I need the last clause?
phrases.notes: This is the case in the משנה where the man writes the גט for whichever of his wives he will later decide to divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since 'לה' already teaches לשמה, the גמרא asks what the last case of the משנה adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new rule does the last case of the משנה teach beyond the basic requirement of לשמה?

steps.title: The last case teaches that there is no ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The last case teaches אין ברירה. We do not say that choosing a wife later shows the גט was written for her all along.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that there is no retroactive clarification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the last case teaches the rule of אין ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could have thought that once he gives the גט to one wife, it is clear in hindsight that he wrote it for her. The משנה teaches that this does not work. The גט must be written for a specific woman from the very beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
There is no retroactive clarification. A later choice does not show what was intended earlier.

steps.whatToRemember: A גט must be written לשמה, for a specific woman from the start. Picking her later does not count, because אין ברירה.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that there is no retroactive clarification.
phrases.notes: We can't say, 'Since he ended up giving it to her, it was really meant for her all along.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The last case teaches אין ברירה: choosing a wife later does not make the גט count as written for her.

steps.title: A גט written for the older wife works for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about two wives with the same name and infers that the גט is still valid for the older wife it was written for.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote a גט to divorce the older wife, he may not divorce the younger one with it. So only the younger one cannot be divorced with it, but the older one can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up רבא's lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the גט cannot be used for the younger wife. That implies it does work for the older wife, its intended owner. This is true even though both wives share a name, so the younger wife could misuse the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The older (first) wife
The younger wife
Is able, can

phrases.english: If he wrote a bill of divorce to divorce the older wife,
phrases.notes: Both of his wives have the same name, so the גט looks like it could fit either one.

phrases.english: he may not divorce the younger one with it.

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה הוּא דְּלָא מָצֵי מְגָרֵשׁ בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: It is the younger one whom he cannot divorce with it,
but the older one he can divorce with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה and makes an inference from what it does not say.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written for the older wife is valid for her, even though the younger wife has the same name.

steps.title: רבא: one of two people with the same name can collect a debt
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the inference that one of two men named יוסף בן שמעון in the same city can collect from others with a שטר חוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This shows that if two men named יוסף בן שמעון live in one city, they can bring a promissory note to collect from other people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the inference from the משנה and applies it to loan documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט works for the older wife even though another woman shares her name. Likewise, a שטר חוב works for one יוסף בן שמעון even though another man shares his name. The borrower cannot push away the debt by saying the document belongs to the other יוסף בן שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows / this teaches (drawing a rule from a source)
A promissory note (loan document)
They bring out (present a document in order to collect)

phrases.english: Rava said: That is to say,
two people named Yosef ben Shimon
who live in one city
can present a promissory note against others.
phrases.notes: "Others" means a borrower who is not one of the two men with the same name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a rule about loan documents on the inference of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of two people with the same name in one city can collect from a third party with a שטר חוב.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the case of 'שמי כשמך'
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבא's way of reading the משנה would also apply to 'שמי כשמך'. That reading clashes with a משנה saying no one can collect from people who share a name.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, the first part of the משנה says, 'My name is like your name,' and the גט is unfit to divorce with. Would you say only the second man can't use it, but the first man can? But we learned: 'And another person cannot collect a promissory note from them'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא. He uses the same kind of inference on an earlier line of the משנה and shows that it clashes with another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבא's logic, 'שמי כשמך' would mean only the second man can't use the גט, while the first man can. But a משנה says an outsider cannot collect from two people who share a name, because each can deny the debt. So if the first man's גט works, it cannot be because a shared name is harmless. Some other reason must explain it, and that weakens רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (pushing the other side's logic to a problem)
The first part (opening clause) of a משנה
My name is like your name
But didn't we learn/say? (bringing a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not deny that the first man can use the גט. He accepts that inference and asks how it fits with the משנה in בבא בתרא, which says a shared name causes problems. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if that is so,
the earlier clause that teaches:
'My name is like your name': it is unfit to divorce with it.
phrases.notes: One man wrote a גט for himself, and a second man with the same name asks to borrow it for his own wife.

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי הוּא דְּלָא מָצֵי מְגָרֵשׁ בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Is it only the second one who cannot divorce with it,
but the first one can divorce with it?!
But didn't we say:
phrases.notes: This is quoting a משנה in בבא בתרא 172a about two people with the same name.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְלֹא אַחֵר יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא עֲלֵיהֶן שְׁטַר חוֹב״!
phrases.english: 'And another person cannot present a promissory note against them'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's statement and the type of inference it was built on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule (step 14) and the inference from the משנה that a same-name document still works for its real owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same inference applied to 'שמי כשמך' would make the גט valid for the first man. But the משנה in בבא בתרא says no one can collect from two people who share a name. So a shared name does cause a problem, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: How the 'שמי כשמך' case must be explained
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: in the 'שמי כשמך' case, how can the first man divorce with that גט? He answers that the case has עדי מסירה, and the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do you have to say there? That it is a case with witnesses who watch the handing over, and the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how the 'שמי כשמך' case must work, even according to רבא. This sets up his next move, where he will say the same explanation works for our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two couples share the same names, so a גט could be misused by the other couple. The only way the first man can safely divorce with it is if witnesses watch the handing over. According to רבי אלעזר, those witnesses are what make the גט take effect, and they know exactly which woman got it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what do you have to say? (you are forced to give this answer)
Witnesses who watch the גט being handed to the woman

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
phrases.notes: He means the 'שמי כשמך' case from step 15. How can the first man use that גט?

phrases.english: It is with witnesses of the handing over, and it is the view of רבי אלעזר;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge by showing how the 'שמי כשמך' case has to be explained.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to one with עדי מסירה, following רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first man could divorce with the גט simply because the name fits him.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can divorce only because עדי מסירה see which woman received it, following רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The two-wives case is explained the same way, so רבא's proof falls
steps.stepSummary: The two-wives case is also about עדי מסירה, following רבי אלעזר. So רבא cannot learn from it that a שטר with a shared name can be used to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is with witnesses of the handing over, and it is the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies the same answer to the case of two wives with the same name. This knocks down רבא's inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thought the משנה shows that a document with a shared name still works on its own. אביי says the גט works only because עדי מסירה know which wife received it. A שטר חוב has no such witnesses, so רבא's lesson does not follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too (the same explanation applies to our case)
'It is [the view of]': ties a משנה to one תנא

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the two-wives משנה works only because of עדי מסירה, following רבי אלעזר. So it teaches nothing about collecting with a שטר when two people share a name.

phrases.english: Here too, it is with witnesses of the handing over,
and it is the view of רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי – בְּעֵדֵי מְסִירָה, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the explanation from step 16 and applies it to the two-wives case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's inference from step 14 about two men named יוסף בן שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The גט is valid because of עדי מסירה, not because a document with a shared name works on its own. A שטר חוב has no such witnesses.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue whether the invalid גיטין block marrying a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב says every invalid גט in the משנה makes the woman forbidden to a כהן, except the first one. שמואל says even the first one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: All of them disqualify for כהונה, except the first. And שמואל said: Even the first also disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רב and שמואל argue whether a woman who received one of the invalid גיטין in the משנה becomes forbidden to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט does not divorce her, but it may still give her enough of a 'divorced' status to be forbidden to a כהן. רב leaves out the first case, a גט that was never written for divorce at all. שמואל says even that one disqualifies her.

keyTerms.meaning: They disqualify (make her forbidden to a כהן)
The priesthood; marrying a כהן
Except for the first case in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'פסול' (invalid) means the גט does not end the marriage. 'פוסל' (disqualifies) means it still makes her forbidden to a כהן. A גט can be both at once.

phrases.english: רב said: All of them disqualify for the priesthood,
except for the first.
phrases.notes: The first case is the גט that was written just for practice, not to divorce anyone.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אַף רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי פּוֹסֵל.
phrases.english: And שמואל said: Even the first also disqualifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה: whether invalid גיטין disqualify a woman from marrying a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: every invalid גט disqualifies her from כהונה except the first. שמואל: even the first disqualifies her.

steps.title: שמואל follows his general rule about 'invalid' גט and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's view matches his general rule. Whenever חכמים call a גט 'invalid', it is invalid but still disqualifies her. An 'invalid' חליצה is invalid but still forbids her to the other brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own reasoning, as שמואל said: Anywhere the חכמים taught 'an invalid גט', it is invalid and disqualifies. 'An invalid חליצה' is invalid, and it disqualifies her from the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's view in step 18 fits a general rule he holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the word 'פסול' in a משנה as meaning two things. The act does not work, yet it still has an effect. That is why even the first גט disqualifies her from כהונה, and an invalid חליצה still blocks יבום with the other brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (consistent with what he says elsewhere)
Invalid, yet still disqualifies
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from יבום
The other brothers of the husband who died

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule: whenever the חכמים call a גט or a חליצה 'פסול', it does not work, but it still disqualifies her. That is why he says even the first גט disqualifies her from כהונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule reaches beyond our משנה. It tells us how to read the word 'פסול' in every משנה about גט and חליצה.

phrases.english: And שמואל follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: as שמואל said: Any place where the Sages taught
'an invalid bill of divorce', it is invalid and it disqualifies.
'An invalid חליצה': it is invalid,
and it disqualifies her from the brothers.
phrases.notes: She can no longer do יבום with any of the other brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains שמואל's view in step 18 by tying it to his general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever חכמים say 'invalid גט' or 'invalid חליצה', the act does not work but still disqualifies: from כהונה for a גט, and from the other brothers for a חליצה.

steps.title: Left-foot or nighttime חליצה is invalid but still disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they say in the name of רבי אלעזר that a חליצה on the left foot or at night is invalid, and it still disqualifies the woman from the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say in the name of רבי אלעזר: a חליצה done on the left foot or done at night is invalid, and it still disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי אלעזר. It gives specific examples of a חליצה that does not work but still has an effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper חליצה must be on the right foot and done by day, so left-foot or nighttime חליצה fails to release the woman. Even so, it is strong enough to forbid her to the other brothers, so she cannot do יבום with them. This matches שמואל's rule from step 19, that an 'invalid' חליצה is invalid but still forbids her to the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
Left (the left foot of the יבם)
Night
Invalid, yet they disqualify
The ceremony releasing a widow from יבום

steps.whatToRemember: An invalid חליצה (left foot or at night) does not release her, but it still forbids her to the other brothers. This is the same idea as שמואל's rule about an invalid גט.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Invalid' here does not mean 'nothing happened.' The חליצה fails to free her, but it still has the power to forbid her to the brothers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a concrete example of the 'invalid but still disqualifies' idea that שמואל applied to the גט in our משנה.

phrases.english: In the West they say
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל, where this גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: in the name of רבי אלעזר:
Left and night –
phrases.notes: He means a חליצה done on the יבם's left foot, or done at night.

phrases.english: are invalid and they disqualify,
phrases.notes: They don't free her, but they still forbid her to the other brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel statement from ארץ ישראל that matches שמואל's rule that an 'invalid' חליצה still forbids her to the brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חליצה done on the left foot or at night is invalid, yet it disqualifies the יבמה from the other brothers.
